notes: LUM-1332 — drag-select and copy-on-select inside the composer, driven through a real PTY into the real binary (100x20).

Geometry: the composer is docked above the status bar. A one-row draft sits on row 18, a two-row draft on rows 17-18; the status bar is row 19. The label '> ' owns columns 0-1, so draft body column N sits at cell x = 2 + N, and continuation rows are indented by the same two columns.

Two things a character grid cannot show are asserted through the harness' extra evidence lines: '# reverse y=<row> x=<first>-<last> <cells>' (the reversed-video highlight a selection paints; enabled by "report_reverse": true) and '# clipboard: <text>' (an OSC 52 write the app sent the terminal during that panel, i.e. copy-on-select actually reached the clipboard channel).

The caret is the '\u258d' glyph the renderer inserts at the cursor offset, so 'where is the caret' stays a text assertion. The marker is inserted *mid-row*: cells to its right are shifted one column, which is why a reversed run can be one cell wider than the selected text and why a row text is matched with `.` where the caret sits.

Panels 2, 5 and 7 are pixel-identical to their predecessors on purpose: a copy is not an edit and a click outside the composer changes nothing. Their evidence is the '# clipboard' line, which the grid cannot show.

Panels 1-2 are the drag itself and its release; 3 re-checks LUM-1327's click semantics (caret placed, nothing copied); 4-5 drag across a line break; 6-7 clamp a drag that leaves the composer and prove the transcript underneath is untouched.

Panel 8 is the dismissal rule: a left press outside the composer drops the composer's highlight (upstream re-anchors its single screen selection on every press), while the caret stays where the drag finished.

Panels 9-10 are the CJK intersection with LUM-1336: the composer lays out in terminal columns there, a wide glyph owns two cells, and the drag/highlight/copy have to agree — the reversed run is five cells (你 2 + marker 1 + 好 2) for a two-character selection.
caption: LUM-1332 — composer drag-select + copy-on-select (codex chat_composer/mouse.rs `copy_selection`, upstream pi-ts screen selection semantics), real binary + real PTY + pyte. Panel 1: dragging from the first 'l' of 'llo' to the 'o' of 'world' highlights exactly those characters (reversed video) and moves the caret to the drag's end. Panel 2: the release copies exactly that text — the '# clipboard' line is the OSC 52 payload the terminal received, and the frame is unchanged because a copy is not an edit. Panel 3: a plain click still places the caret and copies nothing (LUM-1327, unchanged). Panels 4-5: a drag across the line break selects through it and copies 'irst line\nseco'. Panels 6-7: a drag that leaves the composer clamps to the composer's edge — the transcript above shows no highlight at all — its release copies the clamped fragment ('line\ns'), and a click on the status bar dismisses the highlight without copying anything (a press elsewhere is a new gesture). Panels 9-10 repeat it over CJK text, where a glyph owns two cells (LUM-1336's column measure): the five highlighted cells are 你 + caret + 好, and the copy is those two glyphs. Nothing mocked.

panels.label: 1. drag from 'llo' to the 'o' of 'world': the fragment is highlighted

expect.why: the reversed cells start on the pressed 'l' and end on the dragged 'o' (the run is one cell wider: the caret marker is inserted inside it)
and they spell exactly the dragged characters
the caret followed the drag's end
it left the end of the draft
nothing is copied while the button is still down

panels.label: 2. release: the selection reaches the clipboard channel

expect.why: copy-on-select handed exactly the highlighted text to the terminal (OSC 52)
the highlight stays after the release
the draft and the caret are unchanged by the copy — a selection is not an edit

panels.label: 3. a click still places the caret and copies nothing (LUM-1327)

expect.why: a click leaves no selection behind
and queues no clipboard write of its own
the draft kept every character — the click only moved the caret

panels.label: 4. drag across the line break: both rows highlight

expect.why: the first row's selected tail is highlighted
and the second row's selected head, caret marker included
still nothing copied while dragging

panels.label: 5. release: a cross-row selection copies with its newline

expect.why: the copied text is the draft fragment, newline and all
the highlight survives the release on both rows

panels.label: 6. a drag that leaves the composer clamps into it

expect.why: the drag past the composer's left edge clamped to the draft's first column
the selection runs from the draft's start to the pressed 'l'
no transcript row above the composer is highlighted
the drag never reached the chat log
an unfinished drag copies nothing

panels.label: 7. the clamped drag's release copies the clamped fragment

expect.why: the release carried the pointer to the composer's bottom row, and the caret finished the drag there
releasing the clamped drag copies the clamped fragment
the first row's run is now its own cells: the caret left that row
and the second row's run covers the caret and the character it landed on

panels.label: 8. a press outside the composer dismisses the highlight

expect.why: the caret is not the selection's: it stays where the drag finished
the status-bar press is a new gesture, so the stale composer highlight is gone
and the click copies nothing of its own

panels.label: 9. a drag over CJK text highlights both cells of every glyph

expect.why: 你 owns two cells, the caret marker one, 好 two more — five highlighted cells with no gap (LUM-1336 columns × LUM-1332 offsets)
still nothing copied while the button is down

panels.label: 10. the release copies the two glyphs

expect.why: the copied text is exactly the two-glyph fragment the highlight covered
and the highlight stays
